questionText: What is Spring Boot and why was it created?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can define Spring Boot, explain why it was created, connect starters to dependencies and auto-configuration to conditional beans, and state where application responsibility remains.
inScope: Spring Boot's relationship to Spring Framework
outOfScope: A claim that Boot replaces Spring
A claim that every generated application is production-ready

claims.statement: Spring Boot helps create stand-alone Spring-based applications and remains built on Spring Framework rather than replacing Spring's container and APIs.
Spring Boot starters are convenient dependency descriptors that provide a supported set of dependencies for a particular application capability.
Auto-configuration responds to the application's classpath, properties, and existing beans, and commonly backs away when user configuration supplies an equivalent bean.
Spring Boot supports external configuration, executable packaging, embedded web servers when selected, and production-oriented features for running applications.

examples.title: Java 17 Spring Boot web application with one status endpoint

validation.command: Review imports, Java 17 syntax, application entry point, and Spring MVC mapping against Spring Boot 3.3.1
validation.expected: The class is a valid focused Boot web example when spring-boot-starter-web is present

visuals.title: Starter, conditions, context, and embedded-server flow

notes: The answer uses Spring Boot 3.3.1 and Java 17 as the repository baseline and avoids claims that Boot alone makes an application production-ready.

review.notes: Core definition, conditional auto-configuration, starter, external configuration, and packaging claims were checked against official Spring Boot 3.3.1 documentation. Example remains honestly marked manual review.
